title: Tidepool Authentication API Deprecation
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/discussions/2596
Originally posted by **toddkazakov** January 3, 2023 Hello, I am the lead backend developer at Tidepool. In December 2022 we replaced our legacy authentication system with Keycloak. As a result, the existing API endpoints are deprecated, but we noticed that they are heavily used xDrip. As we are trying to completely retire the old system, all applications should migrate to the new OpenID Connect compatible implementation. We don't have timeframe for the removal of the old APIs, but the way xDrip currently utilizes the APIs puts a strain on the new system (existing APIs act as proxy), because it starts a new auth session every time it requires a fresh token, instead of refreshing the session token directly. I'll be more than happy to assist with setting up an integration/production environment client for the application. Any OIDC compatible library can be used (e.g. https://github.com/openid/AppAuth-Android). Let me know what's the best way to proceed.

comments.body: Can you provide more information? For example how the new authentication flow works so that we can determine the changes which would be required in xDrip?

Hey @jamorham. The new system supports the standard OpenID Connect flows, e.g.:
- Open a browser to authenticate the user at https://auth.tidepool.org or https://auth.integration.tidepool.org
- The authorization servcer will redirect the user to xDrip using a custom scheme 
- xDrip will receive an authorization code from the redirect
- The authorization code can then be exchanged for an access and refresh token pair
- Access tokens are short-lived (valid for 1 to 5 minutes) and can be renewed using the refresh token obtained in the previous step. 
- To disconnect a user from Tidepool, the refresh token can be revoked, which will terminate the user session.
- Users have the ability to terminate sessions server-side, which will invalidate the refresh token. To obtain a fresh token pair, this process must be repeated from the beginning.

You can check https://github.com/openid/AppAuth-Android#implementing-the-authorization-code-flow for an example how to implement this. I can set up an OpenID client on the integration server when you are ready to work on this.

Is it possible to do this without a web browser? I can imagine that it could introduce the possibility for errors relating to the user's choice of browser component or security issues from the same.  

I get 404 errors on both the above listed auth URLs.

Please go ahead and set up test credentials and send privately to jamorham at gmail

thanks

Something like this?
https://github.com/openid/AppAuth-Android

@toddkazakov Hi, Sure I understand the reason for the approach. I was asking about whether browser is required because normally the user wouldn't leave xDrip to login to anything. Even with google sign-in this is done within the app itself.  

My main concern is that of compatibility that users may have installed or receive bundled any range of incompatible or insecure browsers (for example those that pipe all the data via their own http proxy) - Indeed the AppAuth-Android package has workarounds and lists for allowed/buggy browser implementations from what I can see looking at it. 

This is a potential can of worms I would prefer to avoid but it sounds like it isn't possible to... xDrip does things like wrap the TLS stack so that we can support TLS 1.2 even down to Android 5. I'm not sure a bundled browser on an old phone has the same chance of working reliably.

The url scheme you suggest is fine, however I am also not sure what the implications are for when users have multiple copies of xDrip installed (eg using variants) and how that will handle the callback.

@jamorhan it's not required for users to leave xDrip - if I understand correctly, AppAuth-Android uses in-app browser tabs if they are available on the device.

> however I am also not sure what the implications are for when users have multiple copies of xDrip installed (eg using variants) and how that will handle the callback.

Multiple apps can be registered as custom scheme handlers. In this case there will be multiple xDrip instances registered for the same scheme, so users should be prompted by the OS to choose the one that should receive the callback. I'm happy to work with you on this if you have any other suggestions.

I have added the client with client id `xdrip` which can use the `authorization_code` grant and with redirect uri `xdrip://callback/tidepool`. You can find all relevant endpoints here https://auth.integration.tidepool.org/realms/integration/.well-known/openid-configuration. The Tidepool base url is unchanged - https://external.integration.tidepool.org

Hi @toddkazakov do you think is possible to add a client id for AAPS too? I'm currently working in the integration of AAPS and Tidepool. There are AAPS users that don't use xDrip+ and can benefited to upload directly from AAPS. :)

@emmatovar27 I added a new client with client id `aaps` with redirect uri `aaps://callback/tidepool`. All endpoints are the same as above.

For both AAPS and xDrip, you should include `offline_access` in the list of scopes when making the initial authorization request in order to obtain a refresh token. The refresh token can then be used to get a new access token when the old one expires using an API call to the token endpoint.
@toddkazakov what is the protocol/procedure for utilizing the authorization code?

Here's a rough (and simplified) outline how the authentication flow works:
1. Open an in-app browser at the authorization endpoint e.g. `https://auth.integration.tidepool.org/realms/integration/protocol/openid-connect/auth?client_id=xdrip&response_type=code&redirect_uri=xdrip://callback/tidepool&scope=openid%20data_read%20data_write%20offline_access`
2. Tidepool will prompt the user for their username/password
3. On successful authentication, Tidepool will redirect the user to the `redirect_uri` specified above and will pass the `authorization_code` as a query parameter to the `redirect_uri`
4. xDrip will intercept the redirect to the custom scheme and will obtain the `authorization_code` from the query parameters
5. xDrip will exchange the `authorization_code` for access and refresh token at the token endpoint by making a `POST` request with to https://auth.integration.tidepool.org/realms/integration/protocol/openid-connect/token
6. The validity period of the access token is relatively short (e.g. from 1 minute to 10 minutes, and is determined by the auth server). To obtain a fresh access token, xDrip can make a subsequent `POST` request to the token endpoint by passing the refresh token that was obtained in 5.

For native applications, it's important to use this flow with PKCE. You can find more info [here](https://auth.integration.tidepool.org/realms/integration/protocol/openid-connect/token).

All of the above is generally handled by the authentication library you choose. You'd only need to pass the configuration options, e.g.:
```java
AuthorizationServiceConfiguration serviceConfig =
    new AuthorizationServiceConfiguration(
        Uri.parse("https://auth.integration.tidepool.org/realms/integration/protocol/openid-connect/auth"), // authorization endpoint
        Uri.parse("https://auth.integration.tidepool.org/realms/integration/protocol/openid-connect/token")); // token endpoint

AuthorizationRequest.Builder authRequestBuilder =
    new Au

@toddkazakov With the old style login we would receive a `userid` field. Where is this obtained after using the new login flow? I assume we should be following the same procedure to start a session etc?
@toddkazakov Do you have any more information about how we get the userid with the new flow or am I misunderstanding which steps need replacing with the new authentication mechanism?

@jamorham you can get the user id by calling the userinfo endpoint (e.g. https://auth.integration.tidepool.org/realms/integration/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo) with the access token you obtained passed in the authorization header (`Authorization: Bearer access_token_goes_here`). The user id is returned in the `sub` attribute of the response.
@toddkazakov Okay I think I have this working now. How frequently might we need to refresh the authorization code because I don't think that can happen when the user is not present? thanks

@toddkazakov thanks, that is what I'm doing but I will check the persistence... From what you are saying about the authentication model, if a user doesn't submit any data for a few days (eg they are on holiday without internet) when they return will they be required to complete the browser based authentication again?

Is it correct that the `sub` parameter remains constant for the particular user? thanks

> if a user doesn't submit any data for a few days (eg they are on holiday without internet) when they return will they be required to complete the browser based authentication again

That's correct. The authorization code can be used once. We can set the refresh token life time to be 2 weeks, so this doesn't happen very often. Does this work?

> Is it correct that the sub parameter remains constant for the particular user?

Yes, `sub` is the user id and is constant.

@toddkazakov I have added support in commit https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/commit/e33663e55d34fa7d6622f205096730104359c656 which is available in the Jan 26th Nightly for testing.

To test, the user would enable `Engineering Mode` as described [here,](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/wiki/Engineering-Mode) go to the `Cloud Upload` -> `Tidepool` section and select to `Use Integration (test) servers` and at the bottom enable the `Debug Option` and then enter the details to the `Login User Name` and `Login Password` sections. `Login Password` is not used with the new authentication, but on accessing this preference item it will trigger the initial browser login.

In testing so far, everything pretty much looks to be working and xDrip will cache everything it can until it detects that anything has become invalidated at which point it will start the process again requiring browser access.

There is still an issue that I think the browser is caching the login which means that it isn't possible to change selected user because it isn't possible to logout a user. So if you change the username for a logged in user, it just logs in the old user again. I haven't yet found if there is a way to resolve this.

@jamorham thanks, I'll take a look today. 

The browser stores a session cookie which expires after some time (usually few days of inactivity). To force re-authenticate the user you can pass `prompt=login` to the initial authorization request with [addAdditionalParameters](https://openid.github.io/AppAuth-Android/docs/latest/net/openid/appauth/AuthorizationRequest.Builder.html#setAdditionalParameters-java.util.Map-).
@toddkazakov ok great and thanks for the tip regarding login I will work to integrate that when user name is changed.

@jamorham I took a look at the commit you pointed me to. Is it possible for you to integrate the code verifier challenge to the auth flow as in the example above? This is required for public clients (e.g. native apps) to prevent authorization code hijacking by other apps installed on the device.

@toddkazakov  Please see https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/commit/8e3592e234607b6edfef6c935e2d631f93c09296 for update that includes the code verification and correctly handling the situation where a user changes the login user name in preferences.

@jamorham implementation looks good. I'll go ahead and create a client for you. I'll need a day.
@toddkazakov please let me know when we can test the production side. Thanks

The error said `invalid_grant` - `Session doesn't have required client` - I haven't been able to get logged back in yet but possibly that is because my password has changed since I previously wrote it down. I'm not sure as I'm just getting invalid password messages. Is there a fault with the backend?
